cover.hook: FedNor drops $20.5M into Northern Ontario communities — and Canada just got its National AI Council.
cover.sub: Plus Anthropic and OpenAI both release faster mid-tier models, and another $88M lands on the Thunder Bay–Nipigon highway. Five moves that matter for the Northwest.

reelSub: Five AI and funding stories NWO can't ignore this week.
storySub: What this week's AI and funding news means for a Northwestern Ontario business.

items.title: FedNor puts $20.5M into 22 Northern Ontario CFDC projects
items.body: Minister Hajdu announced funding for 22 Community Futures projects across Northern Ontario on October 1. Over 1,200 jobs expected. Freshly funded CFDCs are actively deploying capital.
items.tease: Next: Canada's new national AI oversight council.
items.reelLine: $20.5M into Northern Ontario community futures this week.

items.title: PM Carney launches Canada's National Council on AI
items.body: 13 members including Yoshua Bengio will advise on AI adoption, sovereign infrastructure, and safety. It shapes how $2.3B in federal AI spending — including $500M through regional agencies — gets deployed.
items.reelLine: Canada's National AI Council is now active.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5: 30%-plus faster, same price
items.body: Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 generates output more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 at $2/$10 per million tokens. Approaches Opus 5.5 performance. Includes flagship cybersecurity safeguards.
items.reelLine: Claude just got 30% faster at no extra cost.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay
items.body: Near-flagship GPT-6 Astra performance at mid-tier cost, released September 29. Available to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users via ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API.
items.tease: Next: another $88M hits the Thunder Bay–Nipigon corridor.
items.reelLine: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol: near-flagship AI at mid-tier cost.

items.title: Highway 11/17: Teranorth wins $87.9M contract for the next 5 km
items.body: Ontario awarded the contract October 1 for the McGuire–Coughlin section between Thunder Bay and Nipigon, with $26M in federal contribution. Two new bridges over Black Sturgeon River included.
items.reelLine: $88M more into the Thunder Bay–Nipigon highway corridor.

summary.title: AI governance landed, regional capital flowed, and the middle of the model market got stronger
summary.body: This week: a federal AI council took shape, $20.5M went directly into Northern Ontario communities, and both Anthropic and OpenAI released capable new mid-tier models. The region has a stake in all three moves.

captions.carousel: This week in AI and NWO: FedNor put $20.5M into 22 Community Futures projects across Northern Ontario, projecting 1,200-plus jobs. PM Carney launched the National Council on AI — 13 advisors including Yoshua Bengio to shape a $2.3B federal strategy that routes $500M through regional agencies. Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 at more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 at the same price. OpenAI followed at DevDay with GPT-6.1 Sol, near-flagship performance at a mid-tier cost. And Ontario awarded Teranorth an $87.9M contract for the next stretch of four-lane highway between Thunder Bay and Nipigon.
